questions.question: Why does the Moon appear to change shape?
questions.answer: The Moon doesn't actually change shape; as it orbits Earth, we see different amounts of its sunlit half. Those changing views create the phases, from crescent to full Moon and back again.

questions.question: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
questions.answer: Lightning's light travels almost instantly to your eyes, while thunder is sound moving through air at about 340 meters per second. That delay lets you estimate distance: roughly three seconds between flash and thunder means the storm is about one kilometer away.

questions.question: What makes a rainbow appear?
questions.answer: A rainbow appears when sunlight enters raindrops, bends and separates into colors, reflects inside the drops, then bends again as it leaves. You see it when the Sun is behind you and rain is in front of you.

questions.question: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon?
questions.answer: Metal conducts heat away from your hand much faster than wood, so your skin cools quickly and the spoon feels colder. Wood is a poor heat conductor, so it takes heat from your hand more slowly, even when both spoons are at the same temperature.

questions.question: Why does soap help remove grease?
questions.answer: Soap molecules have a water-loving end and a grease-loving end. Their grease-loving ends surround oily dirt while the water-loving ends face outward, forming tiny droplets called micelles. Water can then carry those droplets away when you rinse.

questions.question: Why do shadows change length during the day?
questions.answer: Shadows change because the Sun appears to move across the sky as Earth rotates. When the Sun is low near sunrise or sunset, shadows are long; when it is highest around midday, they are shortest.
